name: Integral humanism
summary: Integral humanism is the doctrine Deendayal Upadhyaya set out in 1965 for the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, later the BJP. It treats the nation as a living organism with a soul (Chiti) and holds that dharma, as natural law, stands above the state, the legislature and even the majority. It rejects capitalism and Marxism alike as partial, materialist views of man and proposes a decentralised, swadeshi economy that guarantees work, within a unitary state, aimed at the balanced pursuit of dharma, artha, kama and moksha.
scope: The Hindu-nationalist doctrine of Deendayal Upadhyaya's four Bombay lectures of April 1965 and the Jana Sangh/BJP philosophy built on them, read through Upadhyaya's own text, his associate D. B. Thengadi and adherent economic writing. It excludes Jacques Maritain's Catholic integral humanism, which is a different doctrine, and later BJP policy choices the lectures never mention; those are answered at low confidence.

sources.usedFor: Critical commentary summarising the lectures: dharma above people, secularism criticised, unitary constitution; treated as secondary paraphrase.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The state is held to owe food security, education and medical care as social obligations under a dharmic economy, so guaranteed health care fits, though the lectures never prescribe a tax-funded system.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Lectures insist everyone must get work and a livelihood, and the employer-worker relation should not be exploitative, but no wage-floor policy is stated; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Upadhyaya says competition is destroyed by monopoly under capitalism and treats the profit motive as a distortion; the economy must serve dharma, not be left to the market.

public-ownership.rationale: The lectures say whether industries are state, private or other must be decided pragmatically case by case, so no fixed stance on public ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Concentration of wealth is criticised but no tax policy is set out; adherents are split in practice.

unions-good.rationale: Guilds or trade unions are listed as natural institutions of the national organism, implying approval, but unions as such are not discussed at length.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is described as an institution created to serve national goals and Artha must stay subordinate to dharma, so it is not an overriding right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The lectures condemn monopoly and concentration of economic power and call for decentralised, regulated economic life.

cut-welfare.rationale: A dharmic state is responsible for those who lack means (antyodaya) and social obligations, so cutting welfare as dependency-making is not the stance; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Thengadi reports Upadhyaya preferred production units small enough that those working in them could own, operate and manage them directly, sharing the surplus.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not discussed; dharma places national security high but individual dignity too, so neither side is clearly implied.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on dharmic self-restraint and the moral condition of the individual; drugs not discussed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; freedom is said to end where it encroaches on others' religion, which could support limits, but no speech law is discussed.

strong-leader.rationale: Power is to be distributed and checked by dharma, and even the king is bound by dharma; concentration in a leader bypassing institutions is not endorsed.

state-harmful.rationale: The lectures call the state a necessary institution created to protect the nation; the idea that it is unnecessary is rejected outright.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is not discussed and nothing in the principles settles it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nationalist emphasis on national security and a strong defended state suggests support, though defence funding is not set out in the lectures.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the stress on dharma, family and moral restraint of Kama; sex work is not discussed.

decide-locally.rationale: The lectures call for decentralisation of economic and political power to janapadas and panchayats, while keeping a unitary state; strongly local but not purely so.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not addressed; dharma speaks of both restraint and reform.

traditional-family.rationale: The family is the first organic institution of society and the basis of the integral view; marriage was an institution created by sages to sustain dharma.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; the traditional-family orientation of the doctrine implies opposition though the modern BJP is divided.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from the dharmic respect for life and family.

more-religion-public.rationale: The state is to be grounded in dharma and politics infused with moral and spiritual values, though dharma is distinguished from creed or religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Race as such is outside the doctrine; the closest analogue is caste uplift, which the lectures treat through integral unity rather than affirmative programmes.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed; the organic complementary view of society suggests rejection of a purely constructed view.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The lectures state that the root cause of India's problems is neglect of its national identity (Chiti) and call for reviving Bharatiya culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Thengadi quotes Upadhyaya that old institutions must yield and the status-quo mentality discarded, while rejecting radicalism; neither purely gradual nor revolutionary.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; the doctrine addresses national identity rather than migration policy.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalism is affirmed as the basis of the world order; world unity is pursued through nations flourishing, not through supranational bodies.

free-trade.rationale: Swadeshi is called the keystone of economic policy, with ridicule of dependence on foreign goods and capital.

nation-first.rationale: Thengadi describes a nationalism that is not hostile to internationalism, yet the nation and its Chiti come first in the doctrine.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; the lectures hold nations are parts of a larger organism but give no doctrine on intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Borders follow the nation as an organic unit with a motherland; world unity is imagined through diverse nations, not dissolving them.

limit-growth.rationale: Lectures call for regulated, non-extravagant use of resources and warn against exhausting nature, but do not call for limiting growth as such.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Sustainability is a stated principle of the economic design, but climate policy is not addressed in a primary source.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Western science is said to be universal and to be absorbed, but technology must be adapted to Bharatiya conditions and cannot replace dharma.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Atomic power is mentioned as one motive power among others to be weighed on cost and availability; no stance.

revolution-justified.rationale: The doctrine rejects conflict as the basis of social change in favour of harmony and evolution, though it called for a break with the status quo.

experts-over-public.rationale: Dharma is above the people, but expertise is not given political authority in the lectures; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Thengadi says Upadhyaya rejected regimentation from the Centre and wanted plans built up from regional units.

socialized-markets.rationale: Forms of ownership are to be pragmatic; no verdict on market socialism specifically.

land-value-tax.rationale: The lectures leave taxation design untouched, and nothing in dharmic property views points either way on a single land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance is not taken up; family continuity argues for allowing it while limits on concentrated wealth argue for taxing it, so adherents split.

basic-income.rationale: Not discussed; the stress on the right to work implies work over transfers, but unconditional support is not ruled out.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Swadeshi economic policy implies protecting indigenous industry from foreign competition.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Thengadi says Upadhyaya rejected both plan-lessness and central regimentation, favouring coordinated planning from below.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Thengadi reports a preference for small and medium units owned and run by those who work them, against concentration under capital or the state.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Socialism's elimination of private property is criticised for removing incentive; wages and money are not condemned.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The doctrine wants a regulated, planned-from-below economy under state-nationalist direction, so abolishing monetary institutions is inferred to be unwelcome.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Guilds are listed as organic institutions but state-recognised wage and price setting is not stated.

one-party-rule.rationale: The lectures criticise the replacement of democracy by socialism's dictatorship, and the movement was a party within a multiparty system.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The king is described as protector of dharma in the ideal, but a modern monarchy is not proposed.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy is accepted for choosing governments but declared subordinate to dharma: no majority can make adharma into truth.

direct-votes.rationale: Upadhyaya says truth is not decided by majorities and rejected plebiscites on national questions.

workers-councils.rationale: The lectures do not make workers the basis of power and reject class conflict as foundation, favouring a dharma-bound state.

right-to-secede.rationale: Upadhyaya says secession is against dharma, comparing the nation to an indissoluble marriage and saying a plebiscite cannot decide it.

natural-rulers.rationale: The ruler must be a protector of dharma, but the lectures give no theory of natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: No pacifist doctrine; the lectures accept war to defend dharma and the nation.

war-builds-character.rationale: The lectures stress harmony and cooperation over struggle; war as character-builder is not stated.

separate-church-state.rationale: The lectures say adopting the Western idea of a secular state was needless imitation and that the state must rest on dharma, while denying theocracy.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A dharma rajya is explicitly not theocratic, and dharma is distinguished from religion and sect; laws follow dharma as natural law, not specific scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The state is a necessary protective institution of the nation and justice; privatising it is alien to the doctrine.

military-superiority.rationale: National strength is a theme, but military superiority is not explicitly argued in the lectures.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by an ideal and a motherland, not descent; Upadhyaya rejects racial and hereditary definitions.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Upadhyaya states that India never accepted conflict between castes or classes as fundamental and that the Marxist class-conflict view is a Western error.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The doctrine rejects egalitarian uniformity enforced by the state and sees society as an organism of differing but complementary limbs.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Upadhyaya treats all Bharat's people as one national society, so a separate indigenous land authority is outside his framework and no stance is stated.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not discussed; British rule is criticised only for cultural and economic dependence.

civilizational-union.rationale: Cultural unity of Bharat is a core theme, but union with other states on a shared civilisation is not stated; Akhand Bharat is a separate strand.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The lectures criticise individualism and say the four purusharthas must be balanced under dharma, not that self-interest is good.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Dharma is described as the supreme obligation binding even the ruler and the people, and individual freedom is limited by duty to society.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The lectures stress harmony of man and nature and warn against exhausting nature; man is a part of nature, not its master.

limit-population.rationale: The lectures treat manpower as capital and never discuss population control, so no direction can be inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Thengadi says Upadhyaya wanted mechanisation adapted to Indian needs, not rejection of industry; Gandhian rejection is distinguished.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology is welcome only if adapted to Bharatiya conditions and employment; speeding disruption of institutions is not endorsed.

human-enhancement.rationale: The integral person is body, mind, intellect and soul under dharma, so open-ended technological remaking of the human is inferred to be unwelcome.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Authority rests on dharma and the human integral personality; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Nothing in the lectures bears on communications privacy versus state access.

restore-past-order.rationale: Thengadi quotes Upadhyaya as against both clinging to tradition because it is old and adopting Western ways; renewal on eternal dharma, not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The lectures complain of parties without principles and argue politics needs a guiding ideology.

direct-action.rationale: Not discussed; political activity worked through a party and elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Dharma is described as the rules that sustain life, to be applied in every field, so ends and conduct are expected to be consistent, but this is inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Thengadi shows Upadhyaya favoured modern technology adapted to India, so a return to foraging is far outside it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The organic view of society as differentiated limbs treats functional division as natural.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The lectures stress meeting basic needs of all, but nothing about distribution solely by need.

production-for-use.rationale: The lectures criticise production for profit and say production must meet real consumption needs, as in the potato-peeler example.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The lectures reject the surplus-value theory as the Marxist reading while acknowledging capital formation requires restraint on consumption.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The lectures condemn socialism for eliminating freedom and dignity of the individual and denying dharma; class dictatorship is rejected.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is part of the socialist model that the lectures reject as dehumanising.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The lectures link capitalism with exploitation and Western strife but do not state this thesis.

taxation-theft.rationale: The state is a legitimate institution of the nation to which individuals owe duties; the libertarian claim is foreign.

harm-principle.rationale: Freedom is limited by dharma and duty to society and religion, which is more than harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Upadhyaya states that the individual is a limb of family, community and nation and that the Western individual-versus-society frame is false.

conscription.rationale: Not discussed; nationalist duty to the nation makes support plausible.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nation is indissoluble and territorial unity is dharma; exit as the main check is alien to the doctrine.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is an institution protecting the nation under dharma, not a firm serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: The lectures say voting rights without food is hollow, and that every person must have work and means for a decent life.

media-academia-power.rationale: The lectures complain about westernised thinking in India but do not rank media or universities against elected power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racial hierarchy is not part of the doctrine, which stresses the unity of man; not explicitly discussed.

organic-representation.rationale: The lectures describe society as organs and institutions such as family and guilds and propose power flowing through panchayats and janapadas.

total-state.rationale: The state is explicitly one institution among many and not above others; all-embracing state is condemned as the socialist error.

national-rebirth.rationale: The lectures say the nation's Chiti must be re-awakened after neglect, a revival rather than radical rupture.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The doctrine is not expansionist in the lectures, though the Akhand Bharat strand exists.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The ideal ruler is subject to dharma, not personal oaths; feudalism is not endorsed.

bound-labor.rationale: Compulsory labour bondage contradicts the right to work and integral dignity of the person.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not discussed; Western science is deemed universal, though values are civilisationally rooted.

universal-morality.rationale: Dharma is described as eternal, universal natural law applicable to all peoples.

single-common-good.rationale: The lectures reject the individual-versus-society conflict model and posit one integral purpose served by dharma.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; Hindu nationalism generally sympathises with Israel, but the lectures are silent.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The lectures do not address emigrants; the nation is defined by a motherland, but whether descendants abroad can return is unspoken.

revive-national-language.rationale: Upadhyaya's party backed Hindi and Indian languages, but the lectures do not take this up.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Thengadi reports worker participation in managing surplus, but the lectures do not mention democratic votes in firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is listed as a social obligation, but how it is delivered is not stated.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Capital formation through restraint on consumption is stressed, but deficit policy is not discussed.

economic-freedom.rationale: The lectures criticise freedom used for exploitation and monopoly under capitalism; economic liberty is not primary.

rule-by-example.rationale: The dharmic ruler is bound by dharma and protects it; the ideal rests more on duty than on punishment.

national-self-determination.rationale: National independence and distinct nations are affirmed; but secession of regions within India is condemned.

force-without-un.rationale: Nation and dharma come before international bodies in the lectures, so reliance on a UN veto is unlikely to be accepted; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The integral view includes soul and intellect together; dharma is not reducible to reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The state is the nation's instrument with duties to its citizens, so reserving benefits for them is inferred; immigration is not discussed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The right and duty to work are central; welfare tied to work fits, though not stated.

class-collaboration.rationale: Upadhyaya states that classes and castes are complementary limbs of one body and that conflict is distortion, not the basis of society.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural heritage embodies the national Chiti and must be preserved rather than sacrificed to novelty.

dominated-front.rationale: Swadeshi rejects dependence on the West, but common fronts of dominated countries are not part of the lectures.

workers-nation.rationale: The nation is the unit, and class internationalism is rejected as a Western error.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; divided among adherents.

ban-interest.rationale: Not discussed; capital formation is accepted.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The doctrine's unity of mankind and integral humanism contradict legal racial segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state is described as an institution created by the nation for its needs, not a ruling-class tool; class conflict is rejected.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy sources are to be chosen by availability and cost; a stance on fossil fuels is not given.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not discussed; Chiti implies cultural primacy but not a stated assimilation rule.

elite-replacement.rationale: Not a conspiracy theory found in the lectures.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not discussed; the lectures accept democracy for choosing governments without prescribing a method.

national-mission.rationale: Thengadi says the doctrine is offered to the world as an answer to the West, but spreading a form of government is not stated.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not discussed; organic complementarity points toward rejection of systematic advantage claims.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The lectures denounce unprincipled opportunism among politicians who switch parties for gain.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not discussed; contrary to the dignity of the integral person.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The doctrine says nothing about prosecution of past abuses by security forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is more than a guardian; it must secure food, work and education and uphold dharma, while capitalist laissez-faire is criticised.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Race is not a category of the doctrine; the unity of mankind is affirmed.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The integral man and the unity of mankind imply equal worth, but varna organisation is treated as organic.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Marxist framework is not adopted.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The lectures are about India's own national identity and do not judge settler states elsewhere.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The doctrine rejects separate rights by religion or caste and gives equal citizenship to all, consistent with later BJP policy.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; the later movement is mostly in favour.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; the Jana Sangh did campaign for it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Not discussed; dharma is distinct from sectarian religion.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Marxist state theory is not adopted.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority rests on dharma, which no majority can override; consent alone is not the basis.

trade-surplus.rationale: Self-reliance is urged, but export surplus as a goal is not stated.

population-transfer.rationale: Dharma rajya guarantees religious freedom to all and is not theocratic, which excludes forced removal.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: No such libertarian principle; the state uses force to protect the nation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Upadhyaya states that cooperation, not conflict and competition, sustains life and civilisation and contrasts this with the Western view.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The lectures condemn parties without principle but give no view on banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The lectures define freedom through limits set by dharma and others' freedom, not through domination.

separated-powers.rationale: Dharma stands above all organs, executive, legislature and judiciary, but separation among them is not described.

vanguard-party.rationale: The lectures reject Marxist theory and its party-led class struggle.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Samvit paper describes the dharmic economy as guaranteeing basic needs, with the last person first (antyodaya).

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing policy is untouched in the lectures.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The doctrine prefers cooperation between capital and labour and also protects workers, so it gives no steer on strike law.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Poverty is traced to neglect of national identity and wrong economic models, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The lectures say that with an awakened Virat diversity does not lead to conflict, like limbs of one body.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not discussed; hardly consistent with a dharma-centred state.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Emergency powers are not discussed; dharma binds rulers, but national unity is also paramount.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The state is to secure food for all, yet price fixing as a tool is not mentioned.

party-controls-media.rationale: The lectures condemn socialism's loss of individual freedom, which includes controlled information.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not discussed; contrary to the doctrine of a state under dharma rather than a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The lectures never discuss immigrants or naturalisation.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of elected officials is outside the lectures.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Upadhyaya criticises politicians who hop between parties for gain, but internal party discipline is not discussed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: National sovereignty and the nation as the central unit are affirmed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Constitutional structure is discussed only in terms of a unitary state; executive command powers are not.

clerical-rule.rationale: Upadhyaya states that a dharma rajya is not a theocracy where a sect and its priest rule supreme.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: National loyalty is fundamental, and class internationalism is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The lectures stress moral restraint of Kama but never address censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Terms of office are not discussed.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not taken up in the lectures.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The lectures do not address military alliances or foreign bases.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine does not call for banning private arrangements.

people-in-arms.rationale: The state is the nation's organ for defence, so replacing a professional army by an armed citizenry is not implied; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Thengadi reports a preference for rural agro-based industry to counter over-urbanisation.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Thengadi lists Jana Sangh positions on Pakistan and border issues as part of reawakening the nation's unity.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The lectures criticise westernised thinking but do not frame it as a university-educated class problem.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The lectures claim Bharatiya culture based on integral dharma is the answer for the West's compartmentalised thinking, not neutral equality.

death-penalty.rationale: Not discussed; typical of the nationalist movement.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Curriculum on sexuality is not discussed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Science is called universal and to be absorbed, but religious creation accounts in schools are not discussed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed; moral restraint of Kama under dharma implies support.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The nation is defined by ideal and motherland, and citizenship is equal for all, not descent-based.

minority-language-support.rationale: The lectures reject special rights on grounds of language; but also respect diversity.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The lectures say no special rights on grounds of religion, and that religious freedom ends where it encroaches on others.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Individuals are limbs of society and subject to duty; Mill's liberal stance is not shared.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Foreign dependence is criticised, but debt cancellation is not discussed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The lectures complain that independence left Western economic and cultural dependence intact and call for swadeshi.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not discussed beyond saying the Constitution needs amendment toward unitary form.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Upadhyaya wants growth with Dharma and freedom, and condemns socialism's loss of freedom, but also calls for discipline; no stance stated.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Foreign aid dependence is criticised; global duty not discussed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Jana Sangh later backed nuclear weapons, but the lectures are silent.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The form of the executive is not taken up beyond a unitary state.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Upadhyaya says national unity is dharma and territory cannot be traded or decided by plebiscite.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is described as an institution created for national purposes, and Artha is subordinate to dharma in both state and private hands.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The lectures criticise the Soviet system as dehumanising but do not call it state capitalism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: The lectures call for regulated use of nature and warn against exhausting resources; acting before certainty is an inference from this.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The lectures discuss India's own territorial unity, not annexation elsewhere.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Dharma stands above the state, so the state is not placed over religious institutions, and no church policy is stated.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The lectures do not discuss the head of state's role in party politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Upadhyaya cites Lincoln's refusal to allow Southern secession approvingly as upholding dharma.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The lectures call for a unitary state with equal citizenship and no special rights for provinces, as in the later opposition to Article 370.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The ideal king is a protector of dharma and resembles Vishnu symbolically but is bound by dharma.

character-from-environment.rationale: The integral person has an innate soul and a Chiti inheriting national character, per the lectures.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Upadhyaya says even the king is bound by dharma, which is greater than the executive, legislature, judiciary and the people.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Forms of constitution are discussed only as unitary versus federal.

leader-cult.rationale: The doctrine puts dharma above all individuals; hero-worship is not discussed.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law on separation is not discussed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marxist class struggle is rejected in all forms.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return is not taken up in the lectures.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims based on nationality abroad are not stated in the lectures.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Dharma rajya guarantees religious freedom and is not theocratic.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dharma rajya is not a sect-based state and religious freedom is guaranteed, so imposed dress for women is inferred to be unwelcome.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed; national sovereignty is stressed, but no direct view.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The lectures treat each nation as a unit with its own Chiti and do not discuss unions of kin peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The lectures reject special rights by religion or language and hold India to be one nation under one citizenship.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority emigration versus local struggle is not addressed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The lectures reject materialism and hold that human development is spiritual as well as material, with Marxist historical materialism a Western error.

ban-cartels.rationale: The lectures condemn monopoly and concentration of economic power and call for decentralisation.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed in the lectures.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Dharma is above the people and the judiciary; the majority is not sovereign over dharma.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for women are not discussed.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Swadeshi and self-reliance are the centre of the economic policy; closed blocs with colonies are not part of it.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Swadeshi suspicion of foreign trade rules is counterbalanced by regulated resource use, giving no clear stance.

moral-incentives.rationale: Upadhyaya values duty but argues the incentive of property is needed and socialism lacks a substitute.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolutionary violence is not part of this doctrine, which seeks evolutionary harmony.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Not discussed; caste is treated as organic, not as privilege.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Cultural education in the nation's Chiti is stressed in the diagnosis of national neglect of identity.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The lectures criticise imitation of the West and the colonial period, not rule by advanced over backward societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: National identity must be revived; the lectures treat neglect of national identity as the root cause of national problems.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences as such are not discussed; the lectures give all equal citizenship.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The lectures describe capitalism's flaws but do not predict its collapse or adaptation.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not stated in the lectures; Akhand Bharat strand differs.

delink-world-market.rationale: Swadeshi seeks self-reliance, though the lectures also say Western science should be absorbed.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Dharma limits freedom to protect others and the integral unity of society.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Not discussed; the Constitution is said to need amendment.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaty questions are not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not discussed; the lectures accept elected governments though subordinate to dharma.

minority-veto.rationale: Unity and dharma are above individual consent, and the lectures reject plebiscite for national questions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The ruler is bound by dharma and cannot claim immunity from it; the lectures place dharma above the king.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Dharma is above the legislature; parliamentary supremacy is not endorsed.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The integral view of nature and consciousness extends beyond humans, per Thengadi, but animal ethics are not discussed.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The lectures stress man's harmony with nature without ruling on animal use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Duty to society and the poor are core to dharma, with Artha serving society.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Upadhyaya was a political leader and calls on individuals to serve the nation actively.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Cultural theory of this kind does not appear in the lectures.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is a Marxist concept the lectures do not use.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependence on foreign aid and imitation is criticised, but no extraction theory is stated.

native-born-offices.rationale: The lectures give all citizens equal citizenship and do not discuss birthplace tests.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party relations are outside the lectures.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Upadhyaya states India has become over-dependent on foreign aid in capital, technology and management and calls Swadeshi the path.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Thengadi lists Jana Sangh positions on Goa, Kutch and border questions as part of national awakening.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The lectures regard all Bharat's people as one national society with equal citizenship, not ranked by descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The lectures criticise Hitler and Mussolini as dictators, but constitutional founding values are not discussed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Lectures criticise Hitler, Mussolini and Stalin as dictators who paid lip service to democracy.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not discussed; Lincoln is cited only for national unity.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments are not discussed; respect for heritage might support preservation.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not discussed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Upadhyaya states that Western way of life and values do not suit India and that Bharatiya institutions must grow from its own Chiti.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not discussed; the party worked within a constitutional system.

paid-care-work.rationale: Not discussed; family is valued but payment of domestic labour is not addressed.

filial-duty.rationale: The family is described as a core organic institution sustained by dharma, with duty binding its members.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service recruitment is not discussed.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Swadeshi and criticism of dependence on foreign capital imply guarding strategic industries.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Upadhyaya likens old Hindu marriage, which could not be dissolved by will but only by dharma, to the nation, endorsing its indissolubility.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding mandates for elected leaders are not discussed.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not discussed; property is treated pragmatically.

single-official-language.rationale: The lectures do not discuss language policy; the party favoured Hindi but adherents differ.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from swadeshi and the nation's claim to its motherland; not stated.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not discussed; individual and group rights differ from the Western rights frame criticised in the lectures.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The Samvit paper and Wikipedia report the doctrine condemns reckless profit-seeking and mass consumption, favouring spiritual contentment over material pursuit.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Covert foreign policy is not discussed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc discipline between great powers is not discussed.

corporate-influence.rationale: The lectures denounce concentrated economic power, which implies concern about its political influence; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from swadeshi and criticism of dependence on foreign aid.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property restrictions are not discussed.

job-guarantee.rationale: The Samvit paper states the right to work must be one of the fundamentals of a dharmic economy, matching the lectures' call that all must find work.

democratic-peace.rationale: The lectures say democracy exists in the West alongside nationalism and conflict, but do not claim democracies keep peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Dharma is a binding duty; law should be dharmic, but unjust law is not specifically addressed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The lectures say no society has a monopoly of goodness and there are rascals among both Hindus and Muslims.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage is described as an institution established by sages to sustain society.

local-production.rationale: The Samvit paper reports decentralisation and swadeshi as the centre of the economic model, with home as a centre of production per Thengadi.

informal-organisation.rationale: The lectures call for organised institutions and a party framework, not informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: National sovereignty is affirmed and nation precedes world unity; not specifically about courts.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by an ideal and a motherland, with dharma distinguished from religion; the lectures reject a sect-based state.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The nation's independence and swadeshi reject dependence on foreign powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The lectures stress a unitary state with centralised national unity, though with decentralised administration.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Socialism is criticised for abolishing private property, but a community property regime is not described.

defeat-communism.rationale: Thengadi describes the doctrine as an ideological weapon against Marxism, and the lectures condemn communism as dehumanising.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Forms of ownership are to be pragmatic, but service delivery is not discussed.

religion-illusion.rationale: Upadhyaya states that dharma sustains the nation and the individual's integral life, and rejects Western materialism in which spiritual needs are neglected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The lectures acknowledge industrial development but describe capitalism as exploitation and monopoly leaving man a means to production.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Women's equality is not discussed in the lectures.

socialized-care.rationale: The family is the organic basic institution; replacing it by public service is contrary to it.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism is not taken up, though cultural self-reliance is.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small producing units are favoured, but self-governing communes with common property are not described.

majority-settlement.rationale: Not discussed; inconsistent with the rejection of special claims.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Upadhyaya states that capitalism and communism both rest on a partial, materialist view of man and proposes Bharatiya integral humanism as a distinct third path.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Land claims by historical or religious ties are not discussed.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not discussed; no basis in the doctrine.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The lectures condemn dictators and socialism's loss of freedom, and the party operated in a multiparty democracy.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The lectures say a dharma rajya ensures religious freedom, though freedom ends when it encroaches on others' religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The lectures criticise colonial rule and imitation of the West; swadeshi is inconsistent with colonial extraction.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not discussed; the doctrine criticises theocratic Pakistan and Khilafat in the lectures.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Dharma rajya is not theocratic and rulers are held to dharma, not sect law; removal by force of rulers is not endorsed.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Thengadi reports worker participation in production units and local plans from below, but not direct democracy.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not discussed; class and identity conflicts are rejected as foundations.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The lectures never mention gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from respect for life and dharma.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Wikipedia reports the doctrine seeks a middle ground between capitalism and socialism, judging each on its merits, which rejects a left-right choice; adherents do not say the division is obsolete in so many words.

alienated-labor.rationale: The Samvit paper reports the doctrine says capitalism reduces the human being to a means of production, and communism turns him into a cog.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Dharma is described as above the ruler and the people, even greater than God in the lectures' phrasing, with the king as its protector.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Dress in state institutions is not discussed.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment law is not discussed.

social-market-economy.rationale: The lectures reject both laissez-faire and state control but do not endorse the social market model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The state exists to protect the nation, which requires force; lectures defend defence of dharma.

rich-first.rationale: Upadhyaya criticises concentration of wealth and the idea that a few should prosper first in the capitalist model.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Succession of rulers is not discussed.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Not discussed beyond criticism of foreign aid dependence.

property-franchise.rationale: The lectures accept universal franchise and say voting without food is hollow; no property test.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory does not appear in the lectures.

reification.rationale: The paper reports the doctrine criticises measuring everything in money, which is near but not the same claim.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Not discussed; the lectures note democracy leaves real power with those who led the revolution.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The ruler is bound by dharma, yet rule by promulgated law is not spelled out.

racial-franchise.rationale: The lectures call for equal citizenship for all regardless of religion, language or caste.

online-participation.rationale: Digital participation does not appear in the 1965 lectures.

open-government-data.rationale: Publication of decision records is not discussed.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; later Hindu nationalist groups mostly support it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The lectures say no society has a monopoly of goodness and affirm religious freedom.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition and deliberative bodies are not discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Thengadi says Upadhyaya reinterpreted Sanatana dharma for modern times and wanted old institutions that outlived utility discarded.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The lectures say concentration of economic power under capitalism leads to monopoly and exploitation of the individual.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Sexuality in the military is not discussed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The lectures criticise the Western and socialist neglect of the spiritual; dharma underpins the state.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The state is a necessary protective institution of the nation and enforces dharma.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The lectures reject communal rights and hold a single nation with one citizenship.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not discussed; the state is to secure basic needs, though society's institutions share duties.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy does not appear in the lectures.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Authority within marriage is not discussed.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the nation-first concept of citizenship.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The RSS shakhas, considered by Upadhyaya the infrastructure of the ideal nation, train youth in disciplined groups.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign bases are not discussed, though dependence on foreigners is criticised.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Official recognition of past killings is not discussed.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Thengadi says Upadhyaya wanted workers to share in managing surplus and treated manpower as capital, favouring reward for labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The state exists to protect the nation and defence of dharma is a duty.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Upadhyaya argues that nations persist through Chiti across ages and that India's national identity has a continuous ancient culture.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Theories of sex are not discussed in the lectures.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory is outside the lectures.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The nation is treated as a living organism with a soul, so sacrifice for it fits, though honouring martyrs is not stated.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Wikipedia notes the insistence on infusing moral and spiritual values into politics, but not a good-versus-evil struggle.

culture-before-state.rationale: The lectures say that the nation's soul and culture (Chiti) come first and the state is merely an institution it creates.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology of God's gender is not discussed.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Feminist scriptural criticism is not discussed.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Ethnic ownership of the economy is not discussed; all citizens have equal standing in the lectures.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Merging regions for one people is not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Union independence from party and state is not discussed.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Ownership forms are to be decided pragmatically.

municipal-property.rationale: Not discussed; decentralisation is stressed but not communal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The lectures want a unitary state with decentralised executive powers, not a confederation.

family-wage.rationale: The lectures call for work and a livelihood sufficient for the worker; the family wage is not stated.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity does not appear in the 1965 lectures.

person-over-state.rationale: The doctrine insists on the integral man whose body, mind, intellect and soul the state must serve, while the individual is also a limb of the nation.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Upadhyaya says humans have body, mind, intellect and soul with four aims, dharma, artha, kama and moksha, and criticises Western systems for serving only material needs.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The lectures propose a unitary state with provincial powers distributed from the centre, not federal guarantees.

dense-cities.rationale: The doctrine worries about over-urbanisation and prefers rural industry.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Race is not a political unit in the doctrine, which uses a nation of one citizenship.

racial-pride.rationale: Racial pride is not a category of the doctrine, which stresses national culture.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The lectures defend the nation but do not limit force to defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by an ideal and motherland, with language differences compatible with unity, per the lectures.

communal-electorates.rationale: The lectures say India gave no special rights on the basis of religion, language, province or caste and gave all equal citizenship.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not discussed; the lectures criticise only internal neglect of identity.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; Upadhyaya says there are good and bad people in every community and affirms religious freedom, while criticising theocratic Pakistan, so a stated incompatibility claim is not supported.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Lectures never address pollution pricing; the stress on harmony with nature and decentralised swadeshi economy does not settle taxes versus regulation.

future-generations.rationale: The nation is conceived as a living organism with a continuing soul and dharma upholds it across time, so duties to descendants are inferred; no direct statement.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed in the lectures; adherents are split between complementary-role views of women's nature and equal-participation views.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not discussed in the lectures; the doctrine's emphasis on a strong, self-reliant nation implies keeping arms as the nation sees fit, an inference.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not stated; the doctrine treats national interest as paramount and nothing suggests renouncing confidential negotiation, so the claim is inferred to be rejected.

capital-controls.rationale: Swadeshi and economic self-reliance, with the state guarding national economic interests, imply limiting foreign capital's reach, though no explicit rule on capital flows is given.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A unitary dharmic state that guarantees order is implied, though the lectures never discuss arms control; inferred from the state's role as guardian of dharma.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The doctrine prizes national defence and duty to the nation, so refusing orders to fight is unlikely; inferred, not stated.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Upadhyaya's economy guarantees work and a fair wage and values labour's place in society, so collective settlement fits; the lectures do not name bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The doctrine guarantees minimum work and living but does not address tax-credit mechanisms; adherents' views on them are unrecorded.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The lectures are silent on fiscal rules; swadeshi self-reliance suggests thrift while state-guaranteed work suggests spending, so the inference is split.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Opposition to both capitalism and imperial-era dependence implies sympathy for a fairer world economy, inferred from swadeshi self-reliance.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Integral humanism builds on the existing nation and its continuity, rejecting Marxist revolution; this is an inference from its anti-class-struggle stance.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The lectures stress a decentralised but single national economy rooted in Indian culture, not a free-for-all of competing systems; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Its holistic view of man and nature, in which man is part of an integrated whole, suggests valuing natural resources; the economic accounting framing is not stated.

sacred-nation.rationale: The lectures hold the nation to be a living organism with a soul (Chiti) that persists beyond individuals and gives them meaning.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The doctrine predates student loans and has no stated position; adherents' views are unrecorded.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The lectures call for decentralisation and balanced regional development but do not use a colonial analogy; inferred and split.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The lectures hold that man has an integrated body, mind, intellect and soul with an enduring dharmic nature, which implies a fixed human nature, though redesign is never discussed.

public-service-media.rationale: The doctrine does not address media funding; adherents split between public funding and distrust of state-run media.

missingStatements.text: There is a moral law that stands above the ruler, the legislature and the majority, and no vote can make it void.
missingStatements.rationale: Upadhyaya states dharma is higher than the executive, legislature, judiciary and the people, so that even a near-unanimous vote against it does not make it truth.

missingStatements.text: A nation has a collective soul or character that gives its culture continuity and decides what belongs in it.
missingStatements.rationale: The doctrine's core idea of Chiti is the soul of the nation, which shapes culture and filters what is accepted, and neglect of it is called the root cause of national problems.

notes: The lectures say little on social issues, immigration, gender and foreign policy, so many answers are low-confidence inferences. Adherents of the later BJP differ widely on social questions; this profile follows the 1965 text. Upadhyaya's view of castes as complementary limbs of one body is stated, but modern adherents differ on caste.
